clue.text: Son turning over loft space finds familiar form of dish

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: turning over tells us to read the following pair of words' synonyms backwards together

parts.note: to loft a ball is to lob it high
a space is a gap

explanation.surface: Someone clearing out the attic with their son comes across a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loft' is not an attic but a verb from tennis or cricket; 'turning over' turns both synonyms round as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Spag bol is the casual British shortening of spaghetti bolognese, a familiar version of the dish's name.

clue.text: In which one serves or receives drink

definitions.text: In which one serves or receives
definitions.meaning: a racket game with serves and returns
a fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.definitionFit: Squash names both the racket sport played against walls and a diluted fruit drink.

clue.text: First couple of lignite blocks rot beneath a ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts the following piece below a
blocks means sits in the middle of another piece

parts.note: bosh is nonsense, rot

indicators.note: takes the opening two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Coal blocks rot at the bottom of a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of it, to abolish it.

clue.text: Welfare reformer picked up something for supper

indicators.note: picked up as heard, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: a beverage is a drink, something taken with supper

explanation.surface: A social reformer collects a snack for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: William Beveridge's 1942 report founded the British welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: Beveridge was the architect of the UK welfare state, a famous reformer.

clue.text: Composer's one all-vocal medley

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, signalling the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is a choral medley sung entirely a cappella.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruggero Leoncavallo wrote the opera Pagliacci, so is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Reason given victim of corporal punishment?

definitions.meaning: to be given ... is to be punished or scolded, as a caned pupil was

explanation.surface: A teacher explains why a pupil was caned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a question demanding a reason and an idiom for a severe telling-off or beating.

clue.text: Is no longer dated: making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback suggests going back the other way

parts.note: to date someone is to see them, past tense saw

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned style is returning to fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Was is the past tense of is, so describes what is no longer.

clue.text: Table salt's almost completely over

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
almost drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: all means completely
a salt is a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A dining table is nearly covered in spilt salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is an old sailor, not table salt; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the communion table in a church.

clue.text: A good way to leave stocking drawer: it's a mess!

indicators.note: stocking means keeping inside, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: a good way off is far
to go is to leave
an RA, Royal Academician, is an artist, one who draws

explanation.surface: Someone tries to escape from a drawer full of tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' and 'drawer' suggest underwear; a drawer is one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble, a mess.

clue.text: Char lady

definitions.meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for tea, also called char

explanation.definitionFit: Rosie Lee is rhyming slang for tea, informally char, and also looks like a woman's name.

clue.text: Obscure bigwig put in tanner, with notes still to pay

indicators.note: put in signals one piece placed inside another here

parts.note: UV, ultraviolet light, is what tans the skin
a nob is a toff or important person
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts still owed

explanation.surface: A grandee hides in a sunbed salon while his debts pile up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is also an old British sixpence coin, which helps the misdirection; here it is ultraviolet light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is not apparent or plain, which is a synonym for not obvious.

clue.text: Hookers finding way back on pitch

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: pitch is tar, the black sticky substance

indicators.note: back says the street abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Prostitutes return to their usual street patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a street-walker's patch, but it is tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hookers and tarts are both slang words for prostitutes.

clue.text: Sportsman risked playing cut

indicators.note: playing suggests letters being played about with and rearranged
cut means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A daring athlete gambled and lost his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims RISKED to RISKE, and 'playing' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a sportsman who races or travels on skis.

clue.text: Wacky baccy free in surfer's paradise?

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, a sign the letters go mad and reshuffle

explanation.surface: A beach bum dreams of free cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: BACCY is British slang for tobacco, and wacky baccy is cannabis; the surfer is one on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A web surfer would find heaven in a café offering internet access, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sweet is enticement to go round grandmother's place

indicators.note: go round means surround another piece

parts.note: bait is a lure
nana is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Treats are used to lure people round to Granny's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Novel painting, fake, possessed by you

indicators.note: possessed by means held within the outer piece

parts.note: thee is the archaic form of you
a da Vinci is a painting by Leonardo
cod means sham or fake, as in cod Latin

explanation.surface: A forged painting is owned by the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Brown's bestseller is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Tiny bit of leeway I allow settler

parts.note: 1 mm, one millimetre, is a tiny allowance of space
to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone grants a newcomer a little latitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 1 of 1 mm as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is a person who comes to settle in a new country.

clue.text: One falling spectacularly for the hero?

definitions.text: One falling spectacularly for the hero?

parts.words: One falling spectacularly for the hero?
parts.note: seems to be a besotted admirer, but means someone who does the dramatic falls in place of a film's lead actor

explanation.definitionFit: A stunt double takes the dangerous falls on behalf of the star playing the hero.

clue.text: Proverbial crowd of ignorant cowards tailed by the Dutch?

parts.note: two's company, three's a crowd
blind means unaware or ignorant
mice are timid creatures, so cowards

explanation.surface: Dutch people are accused of being an ignorant cowardly mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is rhyming slang for wife (Duchess of Fife); in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme creatures famously had their tails cut off by the farmer's spouse, here called the Dutch.

clue.text: Author's brief, unsuccessful innings occupying crease

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside

parts.note: to rumple is to crease
O, a duck, is a score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman's short failed innings at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey is the barrister created by John Mortimer; a brief is British slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpole is a fictional barrister, the brief created by an author.

clue.text: Artist nearly crazy slashing topless picture

indicators.note: slashing means cutting into the middle
topless drops the first letter

parts.note: a scene is a picture

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter

parts.note: zany means crazy

explanation.surface: A deranged artist slashes a picture of a topless figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' makes ZAN, 'topless' makes CENE, and ZAN cuts into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cézanne was a French post-impressionist painter.

clue.text: Lacking interest so force bank to keep variable amount

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it safe within, so the bank word holds the variable inside it

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A bank is forced to retain a fluctuating sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something greyly is doing it in a dull way, lacking interest.

clue.text: Delivery smothered in labels indicates important contacts

indicators.note: smothered in means wrapped inside another piece

parts.note: names are labels for things
a drop is a delivery of goods

explanation.surface: A parcel buried under sticky labels reveals who matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray S before labels; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Name-drops are mentions of famous acquaintances, used to suggest one has important contacts.

clue.text: Hang out tops to dry, with extra long line

indicators.note: tops are the first letters in a down clue

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions say peg up tops on a long washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or hang out there.

clue.text: Glass fitter hasn't left one with a view

indicators.note: hasn't left means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a glazer fits glass, like a glazier

explanation.surface: The window fitter has stayed put, a man with a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazer is someone looking at a view.

clue.text: Footballer with another helping to trap ball

indicators.note: to trap means to enclose within

parts.note: more, as in asking for more food
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: A footballer asks for seconds while trapping the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Moore captained England to the 1966 World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby Moore is a famous English footballer, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Place oily clay urns centrally in locker

indicators.note: in places the middle letters inside the locking word

parts.note: a key locks things

indicators.note: centrally takes the central letters of each word

explanation.surface: Someone stows greasy clay pots in a locker.
explanation.definitionFit: Killarney is a town in County Kerry, Ireland, an example of a place.

clue.text: Sort of gloves to have on

definitions.meaning: ... gloves are made of young goat leather

explanation.definitionFit: Kid is goatskin leather for fine gloves, and also means to tease or trick someone.

clue.text: Angry message from one hunting flasher?

definitions.meaning: someone searching for a flashing light-emitting diode would say '...'

explanation.surface: Someone angrily reports a man who exposed himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being needled means being provoked into annoyance, so angry.

clue.text: Talent keeps Queen rocking

indicators.note: keeps means holds another piece inside

parts.note: talent and totty are British slang for attractive women
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Gifted performers keep a rock band called Queen going.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means unsteady, so rocking on one's feet.
